observation.description: The two membership idioms have silently different negative semantics. A declarative live query with membership: [table.hasRole(membershipResource.arg('workspaceId'), 'host', 'member')] RESOLVES for a non-member with zero rows (filter semantics; probe: alice sees 1 row, mallory resolves with 0). A JS handler using ctx.permissions.<m>.requireRole REFUSES with the uniform SNAPBACK_AUTH_PERMISSION_DENIED. Neither discloses data, but a builder switching between idioms silently changes the outsider contract from 'empty notebook' to 'denied', which changes UI behavior, cache/retention classification, and what a probing outsider learns (an empty result confirms the endpoint exists and accepts the id shape). Nothing in scoped-roles.md states the filter-vs-deny distinction.

competitorOutcome.description: Firestore security rules deny (permission error) rather than filter; Supabase RLS filters (empty result) rather than denies — both frozen arms documented which contract they give. Snapback currently gives both, chosen implicitly by authoring idiom.

mustNotRegress: Non-disclosure in both idioms (no rows, no existence details in either negative shape).
smallestCoherentFix: State the filter-vs-deny semantics of declarative membership predicates versus requireRole in scoped-roles.md, with guidance on when each is the right product contract.
acceptanceWitness: scoped-roles.md names both negative shapes and a CI-verified snippet demonstrates each.
